messages:
ryan (Acme): Hey, hitting weird behavior with /v1/rerank — scores coming back different order than inputs and some scores are NaN or 0. Using our TypeScript client. Anyone seen this?
anya (Support): Sorry you're seeing that — can you paste a minimal repro? Which SDK version and which endpoint exactly?
ryan (Acme): SDK @ 2.4.1, endpoint rerank. Minimal payload (sensitive fields scrubbed):
```json
{
  "queries": ["best intro line"],
  "candidates": [{"id":"a","text":"Option A"},{"id":"b","text":"Option B"}],
  "return_full_scores": true
}
```
And response body we get: 
```json
{
  "results": [{"id":"b","score":0.0},{"id":"a","score":NaN}]
}
```
We expect scores aligned to candidates order and numeric floats.
sre-bot: Incident INC-4897 created for rerank anomalies (severity: low)
anya (Support): Thanks. Can you confirm whether payload arrives at our API exactly in that array order? If you can capture the outgoing JSON from the TS client that would help. Also, any console warnings?
ryan (Acme): Captured it — looks like our client is sending a JS Map->JSON conversion when building candidates. Outgoing request body (stringified) shows candidates order is switched to [b,a]. No console errors.
anya (Support): Hmm. Marcus from SDK team, tagging you — could be a serialization ordering bug in TS lib if Maps are used.
marcus (SDK): Looking. Quick hypothesis: we accidentally accept candidates as Record<string,Candidate> in the TS helper and use Object.fromEntries(map) which doesn't preserve insertion order if a Map was passed incorrectly, or somewhere we use Object.keys which sorts in some runtimes. Can you share the exact code you call?
ryan (Acme): Sure — call looks like:
```ts
client.rerank({
  queries: ['best intro line'],
  candidates: new Map([['a', {text: 'Option A'}], ['b', {text: 'Option B'}]]),
  return_full_scores: true
});
```
We used Map for easy lookup elsewhere.
marcus (SDK): There's the issue — our TS client typed candidates as Record<string, Candidate> but accepts Map at runtime; when we pass Map it gets coerced via Object.assign({}, map) which results in keys reordered unpredictably. That can also lead to keys being coerced to strings and downstream server expecting positional arrays gets confused, causing mismatched scores. We'll add validation to reject Map and require an array of candidates.
devon (ProdEng): Also saw reports where NaN appears if model returns no score because candidate id mismatched — server tried to align by id but failed when payload shape was wrong. Fixing SDK to preserve array order should stop that.
anya (Support): Short-term workaround for Ryan: build candidates as an array literal instead of Map, e.g.:
```ts
candidates: [ {id: 'a', text: 'Option A'}, {id:'b', text:'Option B'} ]
```
That should give correct alignment.
ryan (Acme): Ok will switch to array now and verify. Can you provide a timeline for SDK patch? Our CI pipelines depend on the client lib.
marcus (SDK): I'll prepare a patch to throw an error if non-array candidates are passed and add unit tests to assert order preserved. Plan: patch in next release (2.4.2) today, publish canary and a full release tomorrow if tests pass. CC: @devon for rollout.
devon (ProdEng): Agree. We'll add a server-side sanity check that returns 400 if candidates not an array to avoid silent mismatches. I'll open PROD-5472.
anya (Support): I'll keep INC-4897 updated. Ryan, ping here after you test array workaround. Thanks for the clear repro. :thumbsup:
ryan (Acme): Worked — switching to array fixed ordering and NaNs went away. Scores now numeric and match candidates. Thanks for fast triage.
marcus (SDK): Great — pushing canary now and will post link. If anyone wants to verify, install 2.4.2-canary.20260317.
anya (Support): Marking INC-4897 resolved pending SDK release and server-side 400 check. Closing followup after canary stable.
ryan (Acme): Thanks everyone, appreciate the quick turnaround.
